metadata.explanation: Chains the original title-case goal with a new objective: italicize the title paragraph. The getter downloads the docx, checks title case on all content paragraphs, and checks if all runs in para 0 have italic=True. The initial document has para 0 with run.italic=None (not explicitly italic), so both checks fail as negative controls. After applying Capitalize Every Word + italic to the title, both pass for full credit (0.5 each).

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements are covered: title case across all paragraphs (0.5) and italic on the title paragraph para 0 (0.5).
Getter correctly retrieves the file after postconfig Ctrl+S ensures the saved state is read.
Title case logic correctly iterates all paragraphs and checks each word's first character is uppercase, skipping empty paragraphs.
Italic check uses 'run.italic is True' which correctly distinguishes explicitly-set italic from inherited/None formatting.
Metric correctly accesses expected dict directly (expected.get('title_case_applied'), expected.get('title_italic')) matching the 'type: rule' framework contract.
Para 0 assumption for the title line is document-specific but confirmed by metadata: 'para 0 with run.italic=None (not explicitly italic)'.
Postconfig issues Ctrl+S and sleeps 2s to ensure file is flushed to disk before getter reads it.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: if the document could have a blank paragraph before the title, para 0 would be empty and italic check would return False for the wrong paragraph. Consider finding the first non-empty paragraph as the title instead of hardcoding index 0.
